thesis: Same-portfolio growth is material, but profitability and financing through deployment remain unestablished. The bull does not quantify returns sufficient to outweigh losses and valuation.
strongest_counterexample: Pro forma same-portfolio growth of 85% and raised targets show that expansion is not merely acquisition arithmetic.
invalidation_conditions: Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow.
Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of positive operating margin.
evidence_gaps: Acquisition cash returns, deployment margin and unrestricted runway.
Underlying statement periods and forward-estimate dates are not fully supplied.
decisive_factors: Trailing P/E unavailable because the snapshot is loss-making; negative forward P/E denotes expected losses, not cheapness
Same-portfolio growth and raised targets substantiate more than acquisition-only expansion
The pro forma same-portfolio growth measure is stronger evidence than raw acquisition-driven sales alone
